sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ vivyādha bahubhir vīraṃ bhāradvājaṃ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Then Sātyaki, whose valor was unfailing, took up another bow and pierced the hero, the son of Bharadvāja, with many shafts whetted on stone.

sanskrit: sa viddhvā samare droṇaṃ siṃhanādam amuñcata taṃ vai na mamṛṣe droṇaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Having wounded Droṇa in the battle, he let loose a lion's roar; but Droṇa, foremost of all who bear arms, would not endure it.

sanskrit: tathaḥ śaktiṃ gṛhītvā tu rukmadaṇḍām ayasmayīm tarasā preṣayām āsa mādhavasya rathaṃ prati
english: Then, taking up a spear of iron with a golden shaft, he hurled it with force toward the chariot of the Mādhava.

sanskrit: anāsādya tu śaineyaṃ sā śaktiḥ kālasaṃnibhā bhittvā rathaṃ jagāmogrā dharaṇīṃ dāruṇasvanā
english: But that spear, like unto Death, failing to reach the grandson of Śini, cleaved through the chariot and, fierce and dreadful in its sound, plunged into the earth.

sanskrit: tato droṇaṃ śineḥ pautro rājan vivyādha patriṇā dakṣiṇaṃ bhujam āsādya pīḍayan bharatarṣabha
english: Then, O king, the grandson of Śini pierced Droṇa with a winged shaft, striking his right arm and afflicting him sorely, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: droṇo 'pi samare rājan mādhavasya mahad dhanuḥ ardhacandreṇa ciccheda rathaśaktyā ca sārathim
english: Droṇa too, O king, in the battle severed the great bow of the Mādhava with a crescent-headed arrow, and struck down his charioteer with a chariot-lance.

sanskrit: mumoha sarathis tasya rathaśaktyā samāhataḥ sa rathopastham āsādya muhūrtaṃ saṃnyaṣīdata
english: His charioteer, smitten by the chariot-lance, swooned away; sinking down into the floor of the car, he sat there senseless for a while.

sanskrit: cakāra sātyakī rājaṃs tatra karmātimānuṣam ayodhayac ca yad droṇaṃ raśmīñ jagrāha ca svayam
english: Then Sātyaki, O king, performed there a more than human feat, for he both fought against Droṇa and himself took up the reins.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatenaiva yuyudhāno mahārathaḥ avidhyad brāhmaṇaṃ saṃkhye hṛṣṭarūpo viśāṃ pate
english: Then the great car-warrior Yuyudhāna, his face glad with joy, O lord of peoples, pierced the brāhmaṇa in the battle with a hundred shafts.

sanskrit: tasya droṇaḥ śarān pañca preṣayām āsa bhārata te tasya kavacaṃ bhittvā papuḥ śoṇitam āhave
english: Droṇa sent against him five arrows, O Bhārata; piercing his armor, they drank his blood in the fray.

sanskrit: nirviddhas tu śarair ghorair akrudhyat sātyakir bhṛśam sāyakān vyasṛjac cāpi vīro rukmarathaṃ prati
english: Sorely pierced by those dreadful shafts, Sātyaki grew exceedingly wrathful, and the hero loosed his arrows against the golden-charioted one.

sanskrit: tato droṇasya yantāraṃ nipātyaikeṣuṇā bhuvi aśvān vyadrāvayad bāṇair hatasūtān mahātmanaḥ
english: Then, having felled Droṇa's driver to the ground with a single arrow, with his shafts he drove off the horses of that high-souled one, now bereft of their charioteer.

sanskrit: sa rathaḥ pradrutaḥ saṃkhye maṇḍalāni sahasraśaḥ cakāra rājato rājan bhrājamāna ivāṃśumān
english: That chariot, careering through the battle, traced circles by the thousand, O king, shining like the radiant sun.

sanskrit: abhidravata gṛhṇīta hayān droṇasya dhāvata iti sma cukruśuḥ sarve rājaputrāḥ sarājakāḥ
english: "Charge! Seize Droṇa's horses! Run!" — thus did all the princes, together with their kings, cry out.

sanskrit: te sātyakim apāsyāśu rājan yudhi mahārathāḥ yato droṇas tataḥ sarve sahasā samupādravan
english: Setting Sātyaki aside in haste, O king, those great car-warriors all at once rushed forward to wherever Droṇa was.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā pradrutān sarvān sātvatena śarārditān prabhagnaṃ punar evāsīt tava sainyaṃ samākulam
english: Seeing them all in flight, tormented by the arrows of the Sātvata, your army, broken once more, fell again into confusion.

sanskrit: vyūhasyaiva punar dvāraṃ gatvā droṇo vyavasthitaḥ vātāyamānais tair aśvair hṛto vṛṣṇiśarārditaiḥ
english: Having gone again to the gate of the battle-array, Droṇa took his stand there, carried thither by those horses that ran like the wind, sorely afflicted by the shafts of the Vṛṣṇi.

sanskrit: pāṇḍupāñcālasaṃbhagnaṃ vyūham ālokya vīryavān śaineye nākarod yatnaṃ vyūhasyaivābhirakṣaṇe
english: Beholding his array shattered by the Pāṇḍavas and the Pāñcālas, the valiant one made no further effort against the grandson of Śini, but turned to the guarding of the array itself.

sanskrit: nivārya pāṇḍupāñcālān droṇāgniḥ pradahann iva tasthau krodhāgnisaṃdīptaḥ kālasūrya ivoditaḥ
english: Driving back the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas, Droṇa, like a fire consuming all, stood there blazing with the fire of his wrath, like the sun of doom risen high.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca droṇaṃ sa jitvā puruṣapravīras; tathaiva hārdikyamukhāṃs tvadīyān prahasya sūtaṃ vacanaṃ babhāṣe; śinipravīraḥ kurupuṃgavāgrya
english: Saṃjaya said: That foremost of men, the hero of Śini's line, having vanquished Droṇa and likewise your warriors led by the son of Hṛdika, laughed and spoke these words to his charioteer, O chief among the bulls of the Kurus.

sanskrit: nimittamātraṃ vayam atra sūta; dagdhārayaḥ keśavaphalgunābhyām hatān nihanmeha nararṣabheṇa; vayaṃ sureśātmasamudbhavena
english: "We are but the instrument here, O charioteer; the foes have been consumed by Keśava and Phalguna. Here we but slay the already slain — through that bull among men, sprung from the very self of the lord of the gods."

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā śinipuṃgavas tadā; mahāmṛdhe so 'gryadhanurdharo 'rihā kiran samantāt sahasā śarān balī; samāpatac chyena ivāmiṣaṃ yathā
english: Having spoken thus, that bull of Śini's line, the foremost bowman, the slayer of foes, the mighty one, scattering his shafts on every side at once in that great battle, swooped down as a hawk upon its prey.

sanskrit: taṃ yāntam aśvaiḥ śaśiśaṅkhavarṇair; vigāhya sainyaṃ puruṣapravīram nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ samantād; ādityaraśmipratimaṃ narāgryam
english: As he advanced, borne by horses of the hue of the moon and the conch, plunging into the host, that foremost of men, that chief of warriors, equal to the rays of the sun, they could not on any side hold him back.

sanskrit: asahyavikrāntam adīnasattvaṃ; sarve gaṇā bhārata durviṣahyam sahasranetrapratimaprabhāvaṃ; divīva sūryaṃ jaladavyapāye
english: Him of irresistible prowess and undaunted spirit, hard to withstand, O Bhārata, all those companies found unbearable — equal in might to the thousand-eyed one, like the sun in the sky when the clouds have passed.

sanskrit: amarṣapūrṇas tv aticitrayodhī; śarāsanī kāñcanavarmadhārī sudarśanaḥ sātyakim āpatantaṃ; nyavārayad rājavaraḥ prasahya
english: But Sudarśana, that best of kings, filled with wrath, a wondrously skilled fighter, a great bowman clad in golden mail, by main force checked the onrushing Sātyaki.

sanskrit: tayor abhūd bharata saṃprahāraḥ; sudāruṇas taṃ samabhipraśaṃsan yodhās tvadīyāś ca hi somakāś ca; vṛtrendrayor yuddham ivāmaraughāḥ
english: Then there arose between the two, O Bhārata, a most terrible encounter, which both your warriors and the Somakas applauded, even as the hosts of the immortals praised the combat of Vṛtra and Indra.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ sutīkṣṇaiḥ śataśo 'bhyavidhyat; sudarśanaḥ sātvatamukhyam ājau anāgatān eva tu tān pṛṣatkāṃś; ciccheda bāṇaiḥ śinipuṃgavo 'pi
english: With keen shafts by the hundred Sudarśana pierced the chief of the Sātvatas in the battle; but that bull of Śini's line cut those arrows asunder with his own shafts before ever they reached him.

sanskrit: tathaiva śakrapratimo 'pi sātyakiḥ; sudarśane yān kṣipati sma sāyakān dvidhā tridhā tān akarot sudarśanaḥ; śarottamaiḥ syandanavaryam āsthitaḥ
english: In like manner, the arrows that Sātyaki, the peer of Śakra, hurled at Sudarśana, Sudarśana, mounted on his excellent car, split into two and into three with his choicest shafts.

sanskrit: saṃprekṣya bāṇān nihatāṃs tadānīṃ; sudarśanaḥ sātyakibāṇavegaiḥ krodhād didhakṣann iva tigmatejāḥ; śarān amuñcat tapanīyacitrān
english: Beholding his arrows then struck down by the force of Sātyaki's shafts, Sudarśana, of fierce energy, as though about to consume him in his wrath, loosed arrows bright as burnished gold.

sanskrit: punaḥ sa bāṇais tribhir agnikalpair; ākarṇapūrṇair niśitaiḥ supuṅkhaiḥ vivyādha dehāvaraṇaṃ vibhidya; te sātyaker āviviśuḥ śarīram
english: Again, with three arrows like unto fire, drawn back to the ear, keen and well-feathered, he pierced him; breaking through his body-armor, they entered Sātyaki's flesh.

sanskrit: tathaiva tasyāvanipālaputraḥ; saṃdhāya bāṇair aparair jvaladbhiḥ ājaghnivāṃs tān rajataprakāśāṃś; caturbhir aśvāṃś caturaḥ prasahya
english: Then likewise the king's son, fixing other blazing arrows to the string, struck by main force, with four shafts, those four horses bright as silver.

sanskrit: tathā tu tenābhihatas tarasvī; naptā śiner indrasamānavīryaḥ sudarśanasyeṣugaṇaiḥ sutīkṣṇair; hayān nihatyāśu nanāda nādam
english: Thus smitten by him, the swift grandson of Śini, whose valor was equal to Indra's, swiftly slew Sudarśana's horses with his keen volleys of arrows and sounded a roar.

sanskrit: athāsya sūtasya śiro nikṛtya; bhallena vajrāśanisaṃnibhena sudarśanasyāpi śinipravīraḥ; kṣureṇa ciccheda śiraḥ prasahya
english: Then, having cut off the head of his charioteer with a broad-headed shaft like the thunderbolt of Indra, the hero of Śini's line by main force severed the head of Sudarśana himself with a razor-edged arrow.

sanskrit: sakuṇḍalaṃ pūrṇaśaśiprakāśaṃ; bhrājiṣṇu vaktraṃ nicakarta dehāt yathā purā vajradharaḥ prasahya; balasya saṃkhye 'tibalasya rājan
english: That radiant face, decked with earrings and bright as the full moon, he struck from the body, even as of old the wielder of the thunderbolt by force struck off the head of the exceedingly mighty Bala in battle, O king.

sanskrit: nihatya taṃ pārthivaputrapautraṃ; raṇe yadūnām ṛṣabhas tarasvī mudā sametaḥ parayā mahātmā; rarāja rājan surarājakalpaḥ
english: Having slain in battle that son and grandson of kings, the swift bull of the Yadus, that high-souled one, filled with the highest joy, shone forth, O king, like the king of the gods.

sanskrit: tato yayāv arjunam eva yena; nivārya sainyaṃ tava mārgaṇaughaiḥ sadaśvayuktena rathena niryāl; lokān visismāpayiṣur nṛvīraḥ
english: Then, holding back your host with floods of arrows, that hero among men set forth toward Arjuna, riding on a chariot yoked with goodly steeds, as if to fill the worlds with wonder as he went.

sanskrit: tat tasya vismāpayanīyam agryam; apūjayan yodhavarāḥ sametāḥ yad vartamānān iṣugocare 'rīn; dadāha bāṇair hutabhug yathaiva
english: That supreme and marvelous deed of his the assembled foremost warriors honored — that he consumed with his shafts the foes who came within the range of his arrows, even as the fire-god devours all.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ sa sātyakir dhīmān mahātmā vṛṣṇipuṃgavaḥ sudarśanaṃ nihatyājau yantāram idam abravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: Then that wise and high-souled Sātyaki, the bull of the Vṛṣṇis, having slain Sudarśana in the battle, spoke thus to his charioteer:

sanskrit: rathāśvanāgakalilaṃ śaraśaktyūrmimālinam khaḍgamatsyaṃ gadāgrāhaṃ śūrāyudhamahāsvanam
english: "Choked with chariots, horses, and elephants, garlanded with waves of arrows and spears, with swords for its fishes and maces for its sea-monsters, loud with the din of the weapons of heroes;

sanskrit: prāṇāpahāriṇaṃ raudraṃ vāditrotkruṣṭanāditam yodhānām asukhasparśaṃ durdharṣam ajayaiṣiṇām
english: life-stealing and terrible, resounding with the clamor of war-instruments, painful to the touch of warriors, unassailable to those who longed to conquer it —

sanskrit: tīrṇāḥ sma dustaraṃ tāta droṇānīkamahārṇavam jalasaṃdhabalenājau puruṣādair ivāvṛtam
english: we have crossed, dear friend, that hard-to-cross great ocean which is Droṇa's army, beset in battle by the force of Jalasandha as if by man-eating demons.

sanskrit: ato 'nyaṃ pṛtanāśeṣaṃ manye kunadikām iva tartavyām alpasalilāṃ codayāśvān asaṃbhramam
english: The remnant of the host beyond this I deem but a paltry rivulet, fordable and shallow of water; urge on the horses, untroubled.

sanskrit: hastaprāptam ahaṃ manye sāṃprataṃ savyasācinam nirjitya durdharaṃ droṇaṃ sapadānugam āhave
english: Now that I have vanquished in battle the irresistible Droṇa together with his followers, I count Savyasācin as good as reached by my hand.

sanskrit: hārdikyaṃ yodhavaryaṃ ca prāptaṃ manye dhanaṃjayam na hi me jāyate trāso dṛṣṭvā sainyāny anekaśaḥ vahner iva pradīptasya grīṣme śuṣkaṃ tṛṇolapam
english: Having overcome the son of Hṛdika, that best of warriors, I count Dhanaṃjaya as reached; for no fear arises in me at the sight of these manifold hosts, which are to me like dry grass and reeds before a blazing fire in summer.

sanskrit: paśya pāṇḍavamukhyena yātāṃ bhūmiṃ kirīṭinā pattyaśvarathanāgaughaiḥ patitair viṣamīkṛtām
english: Behold the ground traversed by the diademed chief of the Pāṇḍavas, made rough with the fallen masses of foot-soldiers, horses, chariots, and elephants.

sanskrit: abhyāśastham ahaṃ manye śvetāśvaṃ kṛṣṇasārathim sa eṣa śrūyate śabdo gāṇḍīvasyāmitaujasaḥ
english: I deem him near at hand — him of the white steeds, whose charioteer is Kṛṣṇa; for there, lo, is heard the sound of Gāṇḍīva of boundless might.

sanskrit: yādṛśāni nimittāni mama prādurbhavanti vai anastaṃgata āditye hantā saindhavam arjunaḥ
english: By such omens as appear to me, before the sun has set Arjuna shall slay the ruler of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: śanair viśrambhayann aśvān yāhi yatto 'rivāhinīm yatraite satanutrāṇāḥ suyodhanapurogamāḥ
english: Soothing the horses gently, drive on with care against the enemy's host, to where these warriors clad in armor stand, led by Suyodhana —

sanskrit: daṃśitāḥ krūrakarmāṇaḥ kāmbojā yuddhadurmadāḥ śarabāṇāsanadharā yavanāś ca prahāriṇaḥ
english: the mailed Kāmbojas of cruel deeds, frenzied for battle, bearers of arrows and bows, and the Yavanas, hard smiters,

sanskrit: śakāḥ kirātā daradā barbarās tāmraliptakāḥ anye ca bahavo mlecchā vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ mām evābhimukhāḥ sarve tiṣṭhanti samarārthinaḥ
english: the Śakas, Kirātas, Daradas, Barbaras, and the men of Tāmralipta, and many other barbarians, weapons of every kind in hand — all stand facing me, eager for the fight.

sanskrit: etān sarathanāgāśvān nihatyājau sapattinaḥ idaṃ durgaṃ mahāghoraṃ tīrṇam evopadhāraya
english: Once I have slain these in battle, with their chariots, elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers, know this dread and most terrible stronghold to be already crossed.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca na saṃbhramo me vārṣṇeya vidyate satyavikrama yady api syāt susaṃkruddho jāmadagnyo 'grataḥ sthitaḥ
english: The charioteer said: No agitation is in me, O scion of the Vṛṣṇis, O thou of unfailing valor, even were the wrathful son of Jamadagni to stand before us;

sanskrit: droṇo vā rathināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ kṛpo madreśvaro 'pi vā tathāpi saṃbhramo na syāt tvām āśritya mahābhuja
english: or Droṇa, the best of car-warriors, or Kṛpa, or even the lord of the Madras — still no agitation would there be, leaning upon thee, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: tvayā subahavo yuddhe nirjitāḥ śatrusūdana na ca me saṃbhramaḥ kaś cid bhūtapūrvaḥ kadā cana kim u caitat samāsādya vīra saṃyugagoṣpadam
english: Very many hast thou vanquished in battle, O slayer of foes, and never before has any agitation come upon me at any time — how much less now, O hero, on meeting this mere cow's-hoofprint of a fight?

sanskrit: āyuṣman katareṇa tvā prāpayāmi dhanaṃjayam keṣāṃ kruddho 'si vārṣṇeya keṣāṃ mṛtyur upasthitaḥ keṣāṃ saṃyamanīm adya gantum utsahate manaḥ
english: O long-lived one, by which way shall I bring thee to Dhanaṃjaya? Against whom art thou wrathful, O scion of the Vṛṣṇis? For whom has death drawn near? Whose minds are eager today to go to the city of Yama?

sanskrit: ke tvāṃ yudhi parākrāntaṃ kālāntakayamopamam dṛṣṭvā vikramasaṃpannaṃ vidraviṣyanti saṃyuge keṣāṃ vaivasvato rājā smarate 'dya mahābhuja
english: Who, beholding thee in battle ranging in thy prowess, like Yama the ender at the time of doom, endowed with valor, shall flee in the fray? Of whom does king Vaivasvata think today, O mighty-armed one?

sanskrit: sātyakir uvāca muṇḍān etān haniṣyāmi dānavān iva vāsavaḥ pratijñāṃ pārayiṣyāmi kāmbojān eva mā vaha adyaiṣāṃ kadanaṃ kṛtvā kṣipraṃ yāsyāmi pāṇḍavam
english: Sātyaki said: These shaven-headed ones I shall slay, as Vāsava slew the Dānavas; I shall fulfill my vow. Bear me straight against the Kāmbojas; having wrought their slaughter today, swiftly shall I go to the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: adya drakṣyanti me vīryaṃ kauravāḥ sasuyodhanāḥ muṇḍānīke hate sūta sarvasainyeṣu cāsakṛt
english: Today shall the Kauravas with Suyodhana behold my valor, O charioteer, when the host of the shaven-headed ones, and all the armies, are slain again and again.

sanskrit: adya kauravasainyasya dīryamāṇasya saṃyuge śrutvā virāvaṃ bahudhā saṃtapsyati suyodhanaḥ
english: Today, hearing the manifold outcry of the Kaurava host as it is rent asunder in the battle, Suyodhana shall be consumed with grief.

sanskrit: adya pāṇḍavamukhyasya śvetāśvasya mahātmanaḥ ācāryakakṛtaṃ mārgaṃ darśayiṣyāmi saṃyuge
english: Today, in the battle, I shall display the path of mastery taught me by my teacher — the high-souled chief of the Pāṇḍavas, him of the white steeds.

sanskrit: adya madbāṇanihatān yodhamukhyān sahasraśaḥ dṛṣṭvā duryodhano rājā paścāttāpaṃ gamiṣyati
english: Today, beholding the foremost warriors slain by my shafts in their thousands, king Duryodhana shall fall into remorse.

sanskrit: adya me kṣiprahastasya kṣipataḥ sāyakottamān alātacakrapratimaṃ dhanur drakṣyanti kauravāḥ
english: Today the Kauravas shall behold my bow, as I let fly my choicest arrows with swift hand, like a wheel of blazing firebrands.

sanskrit: matsāyakacitāṅgānāṃ rudhiraṃ sravatāṃ bahu sainikānāṃ vadhaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃtapsyati suyodhanaḥ
english: Beholding the slaughter of the soldiers, their limbs studded with my shafts and streaming much blood, Suyodhana shall be consumed with grief.

sanskrit: adya me kruddharūpasya nighnataś ca varān varān dvir arjunam imaṃ lokaṃ maṃsyate sa suyodhanaḥ
english: Today, as I strike down the best of the best in my form of wrath, that Suyodhana shall deem this world to hold a second Arjuna.

sanskrit: adya rājasahasrāṇi nihatāni mayā raṇe dṛṣṭvā duryodhano rājā saṃtapsyati mahāmṛdhe
english: Today, beholding kings by the thousand slain by me in the battle, king Duryodhana shall be consumed with grief in that great encounter.

sanskrit: adya snehaṃ ca bhaktiṃ ca pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu hatvā rājasahasrāṇi darśayiṣyāmi rājasu
english: Today, slaying kings by the thousand, I shall show forth among the kings my love and my devotion to the high-souled Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktas tadā sūtaḥ śikṣitān sādhuvāhinaḥ śaśāṅkasaṃnikāśān vai vājino 'cūcudad bhṛśam
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed, the charioteer then urged on sharply the well-trained, smoothly-bearing steeds, white as the moon.

sanskrit: te pibanta ivākāśaṃ yuyudhānaṃ hayottamāḥ prāpayan yavanāñ śīghraṃ manaḥpavanaraṃhasaḥ
english: Those excellent horses, swift as thought and wind, as if drinking up the sky, bore Yuyudhāna swiftly to the Yavanas.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ te samāsādya pṛtanāsv anivartinam bahavo laghuhastāś ca śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Coming upon Sātyaki, who never turned back in battle, many of them, light of hand, covered him with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: teṣām iṣūn athāstrāṇi vegavan nataparvabhiḥ acchinat sātyakī rājan nainaṃ te prāpnuvañ śarāḥ
english: But their arrows and their weapons Sātyaki cut down with swift, smooth-jointed shafts, O king, and those arrows of theirs did not reach him.

sanskrit: rukmapuṅkhaiḥ suniśitair gārdhrapatrair ajihmagaiḥ uccakarta śirāṃsy ugro yavanānāṃ bhujān api
english: With keen, straight-flying shafts, gold-nocked and winged with vulture-feathers, the fierce one struck off the heads of the Yavanas, and their arms as well.

sanskrit: śaikyāyasāni varmāṇi kāṃsyāni ca samantataḥ bhittvā dehāṃs tathā teṣāṃ śarā jagmur mahītalam
english: Cleaving on every side their armor of wrought iron and of bronze, and likewise their bodies, his arrows passed on into the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: te hanyamānā vīreṇa mlecchāḥ sātyakinā raṇe śataśo nyapataṃs tatra vyasavo vasudhātale
english: Those barbarians, smitten by the hero Sātyaki in the battle, fell there by the hundred, lifeless, upon the bosom of the earth.

sanskrit: supūrṇāyatamuktais tān avyavacchinnapiṇḍitaiḥ pañca ṣaṭ sapta cāṣṭau ca bibheda yavanāñ śaraiḥ
english: With shafts loosed from a fully-drawn bow, falling unbroken and close-clustered, he pierced the Yavanas five, six, seven, and eight at a time.

sanskrit: kāmbojānāṃ sahasrais tu śakānāṃ ca viśāṃ pate śabarāṇāṃ kirātānāṃ barbarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca
english: With the thousands of the Kāmbojas and of the Śakas, O lord of peoples, of the Śabaras, the Kirātas, and the Barbaras as well,

sanskrit: agamyarūpāṃ pṛthivīṃ māṃsaśoṇitakardamām kṛtavāṃs tatra śaineyaḥ kṣapayaṃs tāvakaṃ balam
english: the grandson of Śini made the earth there impassable to look upon, a mire of flesh and blood, as he wasted away your host.

sanskrit: dasyūnāṃ saśirastrāṇaiḥ śirobhir lūnamūrdhajaiḥ tatra tatra mahī kīrṇā vibarhair aṇḍajair iva
english: With the helmeted heads of the marauders, their locks shorn off, the earth was strewn here and there, as if with plumeless birds.

sanskrit: rudhirokṣitasarvāṅgais tais tad āyodhanaṃ babhau kabandhaiḥ saṃvṛtaṃ sarvaṃ tāmrābhraiḥ kham ivāvṛtam
english: Covered all over with those headless trunks, every limb sprinkled with blood, that battlefield shone like the sky overspread with coppery clouds.

sanskrit: vajrāśanisamasparśaiḥ suparvabhir ajihmagaiḥ te sāśvayānā nihatāḥ samāvavrur vasuṃdharām
english: Slain by his well-jointed, straight-flying shafts, whose touch was as the thunderbolt and the lightning, they, together with their horses and chariots, lay covering the earth.

sanskrit: alpāvaśiṣṭāḥ saṃbhagnāḥ kṛcchraprāṇā vicetasaḥ jitāḥ saṃkhye mahārāja yuyudhānena daṃśitāḥ
english: Few left remaining, broken, their lives barely clinging, bereft of sense — thus, O great king, were the mailed warriors vanquished in battle by Yuyudhāna.
